chapter: Jump for Joy, records and royalties
title: Discovering publishing: songs credited to other pianists
summary: Ammons, Johnson and Lewis signed contracts and put their names on his songs until a publisher explained copyrights.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Offa records that I made a long time ago. 'Course I didn't know nothin' about all that royalty stuff. When I was workin' with Albert Ammons and Pete Johnson and Meade Lux Lewis, they done all the contract-signin'. I was just a...just the vocalist with the group. So they was gettin' all the money. I...me, I was so happy to sing, I was dumb to the fact. I didn't know you could get a song copyrighted. I had a lotta songs I...that I made up myself and sung but I didn't put my name on it. They had they names on them. So they the ones got the royalties 'n' stuff.
You remember...
I never...I never knowed what was goin' on to... man...
Do you remember which songs that...that...that you made up that...that they ended up with their names on?

Oh, a lot of 'em. I don't remember now, it's been so long ago. And they was, uh, doin' the different numbers, like we'd go to the studio...what is...Lee's Publishing Company...but a publishing company in New York City. They was signin' up all the numbers
Reel 2

we made. Y'know. So, I got to talkin' to the man one day, an' we's gonna do a session, an' he wanta know what time we gonna do the session. He come to the nightclub. So I told him. I said...we still workin' for Barney...so I said, "We gonna do a session tomorrow 'bout two o'clock."
So he said, "Okay, I'll be there."
So he told me that he want to sign up the numbers I do in his publishing company. So I asked him, "What you mean, sign up the numbers with your publishing company?"
"So you gonna do some o' your own stuff or somethin' you heard or somebody...?"
"No, I do my own stuff."
Say, "You got it written down?"
Said, "No, I got it in my head what I'm gonna do."
So he says, "Yeahhh? Well, I been writin' up the numbers for Albert Ammons and Meade Lux Lewis and Pete Johnson. They the ones that done wrote 'em."
I say, "Well, this time, you'll find out." So, when I told him, "You come up there." I say, "You find out what...who's doin' the writin'."
You know. So I told him. When I got there, so then they asked me when we got ready to record, they wanted to know who and what we was goin' to record. So they asked all them cats. They didn't know.
So I said, "Ohhh, that's the way it is, huh?" So I said...
"What you...what you...what you gonna sing?"
I said, "Where you...where you...where you music at?" I say, "I got it right here in my head...how I'm gonna do it...what tempo...
Reel 2-
an' ever'thing...what I'm gonna sing. I got it all right in my head. I haven't writ down nothin'.
He say, "You wanna sign up for us to publish your songs?"
I didn't know what that meant. So I says, "Whatever...what you talkin' about?"

So they explained it to me. I say, "Yeah. Yeah." So that's how come I learned what was goin' on. Before, I didn't know what was happenin'. I was dumb to the fact. So, I started singin' different songs, told them, "I wrote that. Me. Joe Turner wrote that." So that's how come me to find out that they had a publishing company where you could get money for that.
How long had you been recording before you found that out?
Oh, I had been doing it about ten years.
Mmmnnh! And so you lost all that...because you'd been doin' original material, right?
Uh huh. I didn't know what was happenin'.
